reason: Both answers correctly identify the main threats to causal inference and propose credible randomized stepped-wedge or staggered difference-in-differences designs. B is slightly stronger because it more clearly operationalizes the observational design: comparable or not-yet-treated controls, exposure offsets, an appropriate count model, modern staggered-adoption estimators, pre-trend checks, and concrete handling of regression to the mean, rare outcomes, spillovers, and concurrent interventions. Its discussion of mechanisms and extrapolation also connects the statistical problems directly to why a citywide rollout cannot be inferred from the cross-sectional association.
